source_review.notes: Checked the official ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 record, four SEI architecture-documentation resources, NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, The Open Group TOGAF Architecture Content, and arc42 documentation. Seven destinations returned HTTP 200; the official ISO record was retrievable through source review but rejected the command-line client with HTTP 403. Claims are limited to each publication's stated scope.

evidence: Reviewed stakeholder, concern, viewpoint, view, model, model-kind, correspondence, coverage, and baseline notation.
Checked the interest, frames, conforms, contains, addresses, serves, and typed-correspondence relations for arity and distinct semantics.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation preserves the distinction between a reusable viewpoint, a concrete view, its models, and the people and concerns it serves.

evidence: Executed view-register-integrity with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 4 concerns, 5 views, 4 sorted findings, and ready=false.
Independently traced missing affected-person and risk-owner representation, stale deployment evidence, and the orphan monitoring view to the fixture.
Recomputed Exercise 4 as 95% declared coverage, 75% adequate coverage, 10% time-bounded disposition, 10% stale, and 5% absent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts and ratios are exact under their stated rules; they are navigation measures and not readiness or adequacy proofs.

evidence: Re-derived the stakeholder-to-concern-to-viewpoint-to-view-to-model trace and verified that correspondence rules operate across view claims.
Checked bounded concern coverage and the requirement that every material concern is addressed or explicitly dispositioned while every view has a use.
Verified that multi-abstraction identity mappings can be many-to-many without treating conceptual, interface, warehouse, and physical representations as identical.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formalism supports selection and consistency reasoning while explicitly limiting conclusions to modeled concerns, rules, versions, and conditions.

evidence: Reviewed sponsor versus affected stakeholder, individual versus represented class, current versus transition versus target state, and internal versus external-safe projections.
Tested same-name/different-identity, different-shape/compatible-abstraction, crosscutting privacy and recovery, shadow-flow, manual-process, supplier, and common-cause cases.
Reviewed generated but incomplete, correct but unusable, live but unaudited, snapshot but stale, restricted but reviewable, and orphan-view boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary cases prevent artifact count, visual similarity, generation, approval, or sponsor participation from standing in for adequate stakeholder-centered description.

evidence: Traced decision purpose, stakeholder audience, concern, boundary, viewpoint, owner, status, evidence date, and access invariants through the view packet and examples.
Verified concern-to-view and view-to-use bidirectionality plus governed identity, vocabulary, authority, assumption, decision, evidence, and limitation labels.
Confirmed correspondence obligations across semantics, ownership, flows, contracts, deployment, controls, recovery, transition, and lifecycle change.
invariant_checking.notes: The nine-gate mechanism preserves decision context and cross-view accountability from stakeholder discovery through retirement.

evidence: Reviewed the decision, stakeholder, concern, viewpoint, selection, construction, correspondence, challenge, and lifecycle gates.
Checked counterexamples for one universal diagram, notation-as-viewpoint, sponsor-as-only-stakeholder, framework-artifact completeness, isolated crosscutting views, and source-of-truth absolutism.
Verified that readiness conclusions require semantic coverage, current evidence, usable representations, explicit correspondence, accountable disposition, and bounded scope.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides a reviewable architecture-description argument, not proof that one framework, view set, or tool fits every data decision.

evidence: Audited uses of architecture, stakeholder, concern, viewpoint, view, model, authoritative, source of truth, sufficient, complete, current, correct, valid, prove, and required.
Confirmed that architecture, its description, declared current state, inferred observations, proposals, assumptions, decisions, predictions, and evidence remain distinct.
Verified that the executable checker is labeled as register-integrity checking and excludes stakeholder legitimacy, semantic adequacy, lawful access, or production-fitness proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims are bounded to named decisions, stakeholders, concerns, entities, configurations, evidence dates, and encoded correspondence rules.

evidence: Reviewed source currency, standard and method scope, hypothetical examples, generated-view limits, task-test claims, fixture output, and coverage ratios.
Confirmed that no standards conformance, architecture fitness, stakeholder consensus, legal/privacy/security determination, production topology, usability result, or external review is claimed.
Checked that local conclusions require representative participation, governed sources, exact configurations, semantic inspection, authorized interpretation, and empirical validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Published guidance, illustrative designs, declared mappings, machine-derived observations, decisions, and empirical evidence are explicitly distinguished.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed stakeholders, concerns, viewpoints, views, models, model kinds, perspectives, view selection, data-specific view families, packets, identity, authority, correspondences, usability, access, lifecycle, and evidence as one coherent architecture-description method.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable stakeholder-concern-use matrices, viewpoint specifications, view packets, correspondence rules, source authority, task-based review, access projections, generated views, change impact, supersession, and retirement. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from decision and stakeholder discovery through viewpoint and view selection, construction, correspondence, challenge, and lifecycle governance. Ten examples, executable evidence, failure cases, five exercises, and full answers cover both conceptual distinctions and practical application.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, architecture-method, data-domain, legal, privacy, security, accessibility, affected-stakeholder, usability, operations, or practitioner review is claimed.
